A question to all my Friends on Linkedin: Lately, I have been seeing a lot of
people including some very prominent ones , proposing that to work in Data
Science one needs to master Data Science as well as Data Engineering. I have a
slightly different take on this... 1\. As someone who is a core Data
Scientist, Data engineering is a secondary skill for me. I feel Data Science
is so vast and there is so much of work and progress needed to be made in very
basic things that it is almost impossible to spend enough time on
understanding data science itself. 2\. A secondary skill is a must but it
should remain a secondary skill.In my view mastering both skills is
impossible, one will always remain a secondary skill. 3\. The same applies if
Data Engineering is the primary skill as it is also a very vast field in
itself. hashtag#datascience hashtag#machinelearning

profile_headline: Founder of Spacemen Digital Growth Consultancy | Helping businesses scale digitally | Digital Marketing Head | IITKGP
post_content:
"IIT Kharagpur boy bags annual package of 1.4 crore" - my uncle read out
loudly from a popular newspaper. “Our boy has been a topper all along his
school and college, if not 1.4 crore he’ll get atleast half of it. All our
problems will be solved” - he said looking at me I’m not the first person to
hear these words and I certainly won’t be the last. Parents and relatives
don’t realize the impact of these innocent words. Not even the top 1% of
IITians get the above package. Newspapers publish half baked stories for
sensationalism. I don’t understand why a student’s placement in a Google or a
Facebook or a Microsoft becomes a national news. They just show one side of
the coin. The beautiful side. There is one more side to the same coin. An ugly
side. No one likes to showcase it or talk about it. Be it the coaching
centers, newspapers or IITs themselves. The truth is, an average student at
IIT gets an annual package somewhere between 6 to 8 LPA. And believe me when I
say there are many average students. I’m also one of them. On top of it, there
are many students who fail to secure an offer despite multiple attempts. So,
the next time you come across such an article, take the news with a pinch of
salt. Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur hashtag#placements
